title: Parsing and Validation
governing_sources: specification/volume-ii/contracts/S-07.json (durable handoff and OD-027 boundary, carried forward not reopened)
od_027_position: The OD-027 boundary is established by S-07 (MTX-008, MTX-060) and is carried forward unchanged. The withheld limb remains exactly: a has_one narrowing, a unique (parsing_job_id) constraint, and any second IndexingJob per ParsingJob. indexing-interim-v1 pins both index keys -- ParsingJob keyed by (document_id, content_digest, parser_definition_version) and IndexingJob keyed by (parsed_artifact_id, normalized_payload_sha256, index_target_id=tenant-retrieval, index_schema_version=retrieval-index-interim-v1) -- which is a working interim, so S-08 reaches its outcome and is not blocked. The final multiplicity is not inferred.

MTX-031.interface_type: System automation plus two authorized dead-letter replay commands. WF-006 Actors are the tenant-scoped parsing, evaluation and indexing service identities; the only principal-reachable paths are `parsing.recover` and `indexing.recover` replay.
MTX-031.route: Not applicable - Volume I defines the service identities, the replay permissions and their envelopes but no HTTP path, method or transport. Transport exposure is owned by API_CONTRACTS.md at the Volume II baseline. The pipeline is triggered by an ingestion or parsing completion signal, a retry timer, a manifest-terminal predicate or an intake-close predicate -- none of which is an inbound request.
MTX-031.request_schema: Replay only: target dead-letter job ID, the exact `parsing.recover` or `indexing.recover` permission, expected state version, a 20-2,000 character reason, and a NEW idempotency key. Automated execution takes no request; it consumes the complete selected-Crawl parse manifest.
MTX-031.response_schema: Replay returns the job with its incremented replay generation queued at attempt one. Automated execution produces ParsingJobs, immutable Parsed Artifacts, IndexingJobs, Index Receipts and exactly one immutable Evaluation Input Snapshot.
MTX-031.controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-031.command_input: The sealed ordered parse manifest: the complete set of distinct Documents whose IngestionJobs reached `succeeded` for the selected Crawl, ordered by Source ID, then canonical Document URL UTF-8 bytes, then Document ID. Each tuple carries Organization, Project, Source, Crawl, IngestionJob, Document and input-Evidence IDs, the Source-root boolean, media type, content digest, classification and the latest effective Evidence Validation Decision.
MTX-031.command_output: Exactly one ParsingJob per `(document_id, content_digest, parser_definition_version)`; one immutable Parsed Artifact per success; exactly one IndexingJob per `(parsed_artifact_id, normalized_payload_sha256, index_target_id=tenant-retrieval, index_schema_version=retrieval-index-interim-v1)`; the derived Check-facing Evidence; and one immutable Evaluation Input Snapshot with its `readiness_status` and `coverage_status`.
MTX-031.actor: Tenant-scoped parsing, evaluation and indexing service identities execute and retry. An OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator holding the exact recovery permission, or a SecurityOperator through an active Support Session naming the job and action, may REQUEST dead-letter replay; only the corresponding recovery service performs it.
MTX-031.organization_scope: Every input and output reference is same-Organization, per WF-006 Security Notes. A cross-Organization reference in the manifest is `input_manifest_invalid` and blocks readiness rather than being silently dropped.
MTX-031.aggregate: ParsingJob, ParsedArtifact, IndexingJob, IndexReceipt, EvaluationInputSnapshot and Document as separate roots; Evaluation as the lifecycle subject.
MTX-031.aggregate_boundary: `ParsingSucceeded` and `DocumentParsed` commit together and neither may exist without the validated Artifact and the successful job, so parsing success is a bounded multi-root commit. Indexing is a SEPARATE projection: its result never mutates the sealed snapshot, so it shares no transaction with Evaluation input.
MTX-031.value_objects: ParseManifestTuple, ContentDigest, ParserDefinitionVersion, NormalizationSchemaVersion, NormalizedPayloadSha256, ReplayGeneration, ReadinessStatus (`blocked`, `ready_full`, `ready_partial`), CoverageStatus, SnapshotContentHash, IndexGeneration.
MTX-031.domain_service: Not applicable - WF-006 names service identities rather than a domain service. The evaluation-input service deterministically derives the Check-facing Evidence schemas; that derivation is an application-layer function over frozen inputs.
MTX-031.persistence_model: `parsing_jobs` unique on `(document_id, content_digest, parser_definition_version)`; `indexing_jobs` unique on `(parsed_artifact_id, normalized_payload_sha256, index_target_id, index_schema_version)` -- both keys pinned by their interim contracts. `parsed_artifacts` and `index_receipts` immutable. `evaluation_input_snapshots` immutable with its canonical content hash. The Index Receipt MUST NOT contain copied Evidence bytes and MUST NOT become lineage authority: retrieval always traverses to the Parsed Artifact and Evidence.
MTX-031.migration: Not applicable at this row - the canonical schema owns these tables and both interim keys. The `unique (parsing_job_id)` constraint on the indexing relation is WITHHELD under OD-027 and MUST NOT be migrated; the indexing key stays the four-part interim tuple.
MTX-031.transaction_boundary: Parse success: one transaction creating the immutable Parsed Artifact, changing the same-version Document ingested -> parsed, and emitting `ParsingSucceeded` and `DocumentParsed` together. Index success: a separate transaction creating one immutable Index Receipt and changing the same-version Document parsed -> indexed only when it is still parsed. Snapshot seal: one transaction after every parse-manifest job is `succeeded` or `dead_letter` AND the applicable Measurement Evidence intake close predicate occurs. External submission: one atomic transaction persisting the Measurement Evidence and `ExternalMeasurementAccepted`.
MTX-031.concurrency: An exact duplicate ingestion signal returns the existing ParsingJob; a changed digest or parser version creates a DISTINCT job and cannot overwrite an earlier result. Exact repeated parse success returns the same IndexingJob; a changed Artifact digest or index version creates a distinct job and never replaces an earlier receipt. Concurrent completion order never changes the ordered snapshot or its hash, because the manifest order is sealed before execution. An exact replay against a Document already parsed or indexed returns the Artifact and emits no second transition.
MTX-031.idempotency: Every job carries an idempotency key and a replay generation. Parse replay against an already-parsed or already-indexed Document returns the Artifact and emits no second transition. Index replay against an already-indexed Document does not transition again. External submission is unique per `(evaluation_id, measurement_kind, measurement_set_version)`: exact replay returns it; an altered replay or a second payload for the tuple is `idempotency_conflict` and changes nothing. Authorized dead-letter replay increments the replay generation and queues attempt one; exact replay returns one generation.
MTX-031.background_job: `ParsingJobWorker` and `IndexingJobWorker` per queued job; `EvaluationInputSealJob` fired by the manifest-terminal plus intake-close predicate; `ParsingRetryTimer` and `IndexingRetryTimer` on the fixed schedule.
MTX-031.queue: The parsing queue and the indexing queue, per the Volume I Background Processing action registry. Queue identity is owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row does not rename it.
MTX-031.retry_policy: Parsing and indexing internal retry each follows its fixed 30/120-second schedule: one initial attempt plus two retries at exactly 30 and 120 seconds after the prior failure. Indexing retries ONLY `index_timeout` and `index_dependency_unavailable`; every other reason moves `running -> failed -> dead_letter` at one checkpoint, as does an exhausted third retry. Each indexing attempt has a 30-second elapsed timeout; equality belongs to the timeout and late output is discarded.
MTX-031.terminal_failure: Exhausted or nonretryable ParsingJob moves `Failed -> DeadLetter`; authorized `DeadLetter -> Queued`. Any exact blocked predicate produces `evaluation_inputs_unavailable`, no Check or provider side effect, and the specified initial or reassessment Evaluation failure transaction. Failure and retry never regress Document state or alter a prior Index Receipt.
MTX-031.reconciliation: Later parsing success is visible ONLY to a new Evaluation Input Snapshot and Evaluation; later indexing success advances ONLY the Retrieval projection. Neither reaches back into a sealed snapshot. A successful replay completion event carries `recovery_of_id` and the replay generation and is the ERR-REQ-020 recovery-complete signal.
MTX-031.event_payload: The canonical envelope with the real `organization_id`, plus the job, Artifact, Receipt or snapshot identity, digests, versions, attempt and replay generation, reason code and correlation ID. A replay completion event carries `recovery_of_id` and the replay generation.
MTX-031.event_producer: `Workflows::Wf006` is the sole producer of every event above. `IngestionSucceeded` originates in WF-005 (S-07) and is the trigger this workflow consumes.
MTX-031.event_consumers: WF-007 (S-12) consumes the sealed Evaluation Input Snapshot, not these events. The Retrieval projection consumes Index Receipts. AC-WF-006 states the initial Evaluation starts only in WF-007, so this workflow never starts it.
MTX-031.serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-031.authorization_entry_point: The service identity for automated execution; the replay command for human-requested replay, before mutation. Only the corresponding recovery service performs a replay, so requesting and performing are separate authorities.
MTX-031.permission_checks: `parsing.recover` and `indexing.recover` for dead-letter replay, held by an OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator, or reached by a SecurityOperator only through an active Support Session naming the job and action. `external_measurement.submit` for a tenant-scoped adapter. `measurement_set.activate` for the owner-approval release service. Tenant-scoped service identities for execution and retry.
MTX-031.tenant_boundary: Every input and output reference is same-Organization. Quarantined or invalid Evidence cannot produce a Parsed Artifact. Cross-tenant external content is `F1-DATA-409 / tenant_mismatch`. Input sanitation and untrusted-content isolation are mandatory: the parser consumes attacker-controlled bytes, so JSON-LD remote contexts are never fetched and DTDs and external entities are disabled.
MTX-031.error_contract: Manifest: `input_manifest_invalid` for a missing tuple, duplicate Document, cross-Organization reference, manifest/content-digest mismatch, or a manifest omitting a succeeded IngestionJob -- it blocks readiness and an implementation cannot silently drop it. Indexing first-match before execution: `tenant_mismatch`, `parsed_artifact_missing`, `parsed_artifact_quarantined`, `parsed_artifact_digest_mismatch`, `index_schema_unsupported`, `index_target_policy_unavailable`. During execution: `index_timeout`, `index_dependency_unavailable`, `index_output_invalid`; unknown diagnostics map to `index_output_invalid` and remain restricted. Readiness: `evaluation_inputs_unavailable` on any blocked predicate. External intake: `F1-DATA-409 / tenant_mismatch`, `F1-DOMAIN-409 / measurement_set_unavailable`, `F1-VALIDATION-400 / external_measurement_invalid`, `idempotency_conflict`.
MTX-031.audit_record: Every contract field, the parse and index manifest and snapshot hash, platform-derived Evidence and Measurement Evidence or the missing reason, the intake deadline, attempt and replay generation, scheduled and actual times, reason, failed subset, readiness derivation, non-gating indexing outcome, Evaluation transition, authorization, event ID and correlation ID, per WF-006 Audit and Observability.
MTX-031.observability: Parsing and indexing attempt and replay telemetry, failed-subset identities and reasons, readiness derivation, the non-gating indexing outcome and Evaluation transitions under one correlation ID. A missing or dead-letter index never disappears from telemetry.
MTX-031.retention: Parsed Artifacts, Index Receipts and the Evaluation Input Snapshot are immutable and retained under their own contracts. `payload_retention_class=product_evidence_payload` on accepted external observations. The retention window is owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md; this row states none.
MTX-031.test_contracts: TYP-DATA: the parse manifest is the complete set of distinct Documents whose IngestionJobs reached `succeeded` for the selected Crawl, ordered by Source ID, then canonical Document URL UTF-8 bytes, then Document ID. TYP-DATA: a missing tuple, duplicate Document, cross-Organization reference, manifest/content-digest mismatch, or a manifest omitting a succeeded IngestionJob is `input_manifest_invalid` and blocks readiness -- asserted as five separate fixtures, each proving the member is not silently dropped. TYP-DATA: exactly one ParsingJob per `(document_id, content_digest, parser_definition_version)`; an exact duplicate ingestion signal returns the existing job; a changed digest or parser version creates a DISTINCT job and cannot overwrite an earlier result. TYP-DATA: `ParsingSucceeded` and `DocumentParsed` commit together; neither exists without the validated Artifact and successful job -- asserted absent when the transaction fails. TYP-DATA: an exact replay against a Document already parsed or indexed returns the Artifact and emits no second transition. TYP-DATA: Parsed Artifact content never mutates. TYP-DATA: `parsed-observation-v1` top-level object contains exactly `schema_version`, `canonical_document_url`, `document_kind` (`html` or `xhtml`), nullable lower-case BCP-47 `document_language`, `title_nodes`, `link_edges`, `organization_nodes`; an unknown top-level field is rejected. TYP-DATA: strings decoded, NFC-normalized, internal whitespace retained unless a field rule says otherwise. TYP-DATA: `title_nodes` ordered by document position with zero-based `position`, character-reference-decoded `text`, stable `locator` of `head/title[n]`; blank text is RETAINED. TYP-DATA: `link_edges` ordered by position with decoded `href`, stable locator, sorted distinct lower-case ASCII `relation_tokens`, and either `target_canonical_url` or `target_rejection_reason` -- never both and never neither. TYP-DATA: a rejected or non-HTTP(S) target has a null canonical URL and exactly one reason from `empty`, `unsupported_scheme`, `invalid_url`, `outside_source_scope`. TYP-SEC: the target uses the FROZEN Crawl URL canonicalization and scope versions, not current ones. TYP-DATA: `organization_nodes` contains only JSON-LD objects whose `@type` set includes exact `Organization` or a `structured-identity-v1` subtype; ordered by script document position then object traversal path; duplicates remain DISTINCT. TYP-SEC: JSON-LD remote contexts are NEVER fetched; DTDs and external entities are disabled; malformed JSON-LD produces one malformed item with null name and url rather than disappearing. TYP-DATA: the Source-root payload includes the frozen Crawl terminal-outcome map keyed by canonical in-scope URL with exactly one outcome from `document_valid`, `content_absent`, `content_fetch_failed`, `policy_excluded`; non-root payloads OMIT that map. TYP-DATA: the payload is invalid if positions repeat, ordering is wrong, a locator is blank, a target has both or neither, the root map is absent on a Source root, or a referenced outcome contradicts the sealed Crawl snapshot -- six fixtures. TYP-DATA: one `parsed_content/document-title-observation-v1` Evidence per successfully parsed Document. TYP-DATA: one `crawl_observation/internal-link-observation-v1` Evidence per active Source, combining same-Source `link_edges` with the sealed root terminal-outcome map; an admitted target without a covered terminal outcome is `unobserved`; coverage is partial if the Crawl or relevant parser subset is partial. TYP-DATA: one `parsed_content/organization-identity-observation-v1` Evidence per active Source root from a frozen `public-identity-interim-v1` snapshot whose ID is its SHA-256 content hash; expected public name is the Organization's normalized display name and expected public URL is the Source canonical HTTPS root, and those are the ONLY interim identity comparison fields. TYP-DATA: missing root input creates NO identity Evidence and remains an explicit expected Check entry. TYP-DATA: a derivation or schema failure is recorded by Document, Source and reason, creates NO substitute Evidence, and becomes the corresponding handled Check input error rather than silently omitting the expected result key. TYP-DATA: derived Evidence carries source Artifact and Crawl Evidence lineage and the strongest classification, and is ordered and stored BEFORE the snapshot seals. TYP-DATA: `external-measurement-v1` bundles no active Measurement Set while OD-010 is pending -- the three always-applicable external entries deterministically select no Evidence and return handled `input_evidence_missing`; `CHK-LP-001` does so only when local presence is applicable and otherwise returns its catalog-defined not-applicable result without Evidence. TYP-SEC: no implementation invents a query, prompt, provider, listing directory, threshold or adapter. TYP-DATA: missing applicable Evidence makes the numeric score unavailable. TYP-SEC: an external submission validates authority, Organization/Project/Evaluation, exact set keys/order/coverage/freshness, adapter eligibility, payload schema/digest and one-record uniqueness IN THAT ORDER. TYP-DATA: exactly one `external-observation-v1` per `(evaluation_id, measurement_kind, measurement_set_version)`; exact replay returns it; altered replay or a second payload is `idempotency_conflict` and changes nothing. TYP-SEC: cross-tenant content is `F1-DATA-409 / tenant_mismatch`; unknown or inactive set is `F1-DOMAIN-409 / measurement_set_unavailable`; invalid content is `F1-VALIDATION-400 / external_measurement_invalid`. TYP-DATA: exactly one IndexingJob per `(parsed_artifact_id, normalized_payload_sha256, index_target_id=tenant-retrieval, index_schema_version=retrieval-index-interim-v1)`; exact repeated parse success returns the same job; a changed Artifact digest or index version creates a distinct job and never replaces an earlier receipt. TYP-DATA: indexing first-match reasons in order before execution, and the three execution reasons; an unknown diagnostic maps to `index_output_invalid` and remains restricted. TYP-DATA: each indexing attempt has a 30-second elapsed timeout; equality belongs to the timeout and late output is DISCARDED. TYP-OBS: only `index_timeout` and `index_dependency_unavailable` retry, at exactly 30 and 120 seconds; every other reason and an exhausted third retry move `running -> failed -> dead_letter` at ONE checkpoint. TYP-DATA: a successful indexing attempt changes the same-version Document parsed -> indexed only when it is STILL parsed; a Document already indexed by exact replay does not transition again. TYP-SEC: the Index Receipt contains NO copied Evidence bytes and is NOT lineage authority -- retrieval traverses to the Parsed Artifact and Evidence. TYP-DATA: failure and retry never regress Document state or alter a prior Index Receipt. TYP-SEC: authorized dead-letter replay requires the exact permission, expected job version, a 20-2,000 character reason and a NEW idempotency key; it increments replay generation and queues attempt one; exact replay returns one generation; the 19/20/2,000/2,001 reason boundaries are asserted. TYP-SEC: a SecurityOperator reaches replay only through a Support Session naming the job and action; only the recovery service performs it. TYP-INT: indexing is NOT an Evaluation-input prerequisite -- a missing or dead-letter index never blocks or changes a sealed Evaluation, and an implementation MUST NOT wait for indexing in one code path and bypass it in another. TYP-DATA: the snapshot is created only after every parse-manifest job is `succeeded` or `dead_letter` AND the intake close predicate occurs. TYP-DATA: the snapshot is immutable and its canonical content hash is stable; concurrent completion order never changes the ordered snapshot or hash. TYP-DATA: `ready_partial` continues with exact failed-subset identities and reasons and partial coverage. TYP-DATA: any exact blocked predicate produces `evaluation_inputs_unavailable`, no Check or provider side effect, and the specified Evaluation failure transaction. TYP-DATA: later parsing success is visible ONLY to a new snapshot and Evaluation; later indexing success advances ONLY the Retrieval projection. TYP-DATA: the initial Evaluation starts only in WF-007 and reassessment emits no second start. TYP-SEC: quarantined or invalid Evidence cannot produce a Parsed Artifact. WITHHELD under OD-027 and asserted ABSENT: any test asserting a second IndexingJob per ParsingJob, a `has_one` narrowing, or a `unique (parsing_job_id)` constraint.
MTX-031.rollout: S-08 depends on S-07 for succeeded IngestionJobs with valid `source_document` Evidence and gates S-09. The OD-027 limb stays withheld: `indexing-interim-v1` pins both index keys, and the final multiplicity requires ratification plus controlled Volume I integration rather than an implementation choice.
